title: How trading has been for you lately?
author: tradertojifx
selftext:
Lately I have been having pretty chill days since I have moved to quant/algo trading.Discretionary trading has been such a fuss lately like almost dangerous we can say at this rate.Im slowly trying to improve more in trading and I do know which hours are best to trade too(for me)

Note:I have been trading for a year now,I’m not so good at it manually but recently in terms of algo it has been going pretty good for me

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the calm is real, a rule doesn't revenge trade after a red morning. the catch is that a few good months of algo can be one regime away from its first real drawdown, so rerun it over a stretch it never saw before trusting the quiet. the backtester I'd point you at is one I built, Quantradin. it covers American equities and their option chains, it's free, and every trade is paper. quantradin.com

comments.author: ruby-cos
comments.body: I also moved to running strategies instead of trading by hand. You mentioned you know your best hours to trade. Did you find them from your own trading experience, or from market statistics?

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: I don't trade live myself, so this is just a comment on the approach. The return-by-hour matrix is a good tool, but picking "best hours" from a grid of years and hours is easy to overfit, so I'd check that the same hours stay good in a period you didn't use to find them, and report the trade count per cell. Algo trading helps most with consistency, but it's worth tracking costs and slippage per hour too, since some hours look good before fees. Event days like CPI, FOMC and NFP often drive the best and worst cells, and Cymetica's EventTrader is one source for tagging those.
